entries.title: The Duchy of Narvea
entries.subtitle: Country Profile
entries.text: The Duchy of Narvea Country Profile A concise visual guide to the mapped Baltic country where the story takes place, including its cities, diplomatic legacy, divided authority, institutions, and multilingual culture. The Duchy of Narvea At a glance The Duchy of Narvea is the main country in which the story takes place. It is a large, sovereign Baltic state stretching along much of the eastern Baltic coast, from the approaches to St. Petersburg toward the frontier near Gdansk. Narvea is a constitutional duchy with two real centers of authority: the Ducal Crown and the parliamentary state . The Duke is an independent sovereign, not a subordinate noble. Parliament and the Prime Minister control ordinary government. Sovereignty resides jointly in the Crown and the Nation. Identity Narvean is a civic identity shared across a culturally varied population. Citizens may belong to different regional, linguistic, religious, urban, or rural communities while identifying fully and politically as Narvean. The country modernized without erasing its older institutions. Modern ministries, elections, police, and armed forces exist beside a ducal court, inherited ranks, ceremonial precedence, and a separate Ducal Guard. European diplomacy Narvea historically became a center of European diplomacy. Opposing powers gathered there to resolve disputes before they escalated into open conflict, giving the duchy influence far beyond its size or military strength. During the Napoleonic Wars of 1803 to 1815, Narvea played an important and constructive role in containing the continental crisis. The settlements of this period also began shaping the country's borders into their modern form. In 1917, negotiations held in Narvea contained an eastern political crisis before it could become a revolution. In 1939, another Narvean settlement stopped escalation between opposing powers and prevented a major continental war. These agreements allowed continental borders and political history to develop along a different course. That diplomatic legacy made multilingualism part of Narvean public culture. People in authority are expected to know several languages, but the custom is not limited to officials. Ordinary Narveans may switch languages during everyday conversation for precision, courtesy, emphasis, or habit, even when diplomacy is nowhere near the room. Bird's Nest, the city with many names Bird's Nest has an intentionally unusual name. Most negotiations between rival nations take place there, and every country uses a different title for the same city. Bird's Nest is the Narvean name for this shared diplomatic ground, reflecting a place where competing powers gather without fully belonging to one another. Territory Long Baltic coastline and several major ports Important agricultural regions and trade routes Multiple linguistic, religious, and cultural regions Strategic frontier with Russia Strong commercial and military importance in the Baltic Exact borders remain provisional until the alternate-history timeline is finalized. The two capitals Rennel Rennel, in the historic Narva region, is the seat of the Crown. It contains the Ducal Palace, court, Privy Council, Guard headquarters, dynastic archives, heraldic offices, and ceremonial institutions. It represents dynasty, continuity, military tradition, and the old state. Vilen Vilen is the parliamentary and administrative capital. It contains Parliament, the Prime Minister's office, ministries, major courts, central bureaucracy, and financial institutions. It represents law, administration, commerce, and modern political life. The Prime Minister travels to Rennel for formal audiences with the Duke. The Duke travels to Vilen for major constitutional ceremonies, including the opening of Parliament. Turon Turon is a significant city and the headquarters of MSF. MSF is a fully private intelligence business that sells its services to the government while retaining control of its own succession and internal affairs. A substantial part of its officer corps is concentrated in Turon, giving the company a degree of local power that quietly troubles the central government. If MSF ever chose open defiance, its presence in Turon could support a small rebellion or even an attempt at secession. Officer culture, divided logistics, constitutional loyalty, and the absence of any desire to rebel keep that capacity dormant. The possibility survives in private political calculations because the final safeguard is not an external restraint. It is the belief that MSF officers are decent people. Crown and State The Ducal Crown The Duke is head of state and constitutional guardian. He appoints the Prime Minister who holds parliamentary confidence, promulgates laws, receives ambassadors, grants honours, consults the Privy Council, commands the Ducal Guard, and may hold narrowly defined reserve powers. The parliamentary state The Prime Minister is head of government. Parliament, Cabinet, ministries, the civil service, courts, police, and national armed forces handle ordinary administration, taxation, defence policy, education, infrastructure, economic policy, and foreign policy. Neither side is decorative, and neither rules alone. Security institutions Narvean Armed Forces The national military is funded by the state and controlled through the constitutional government. It may include the Army, Navy, Air Force, reserves, territorial forces, and military intelligence. Ducal Guard The Ducal Guard belongs to the Crown. It protects the ducal family and residences, guards Crown institutions, performs ceremonial duties, and may have limited constitutional-security responsibilities. Narvean Police Ordinary policing belongs to the parliamentary state, most likely under the Ministry of the Interior. Palace security remains separate from public law enforcement. Councils and service rank The Privy Council advises the Duke on constitutional questions, foreign affairs, national security, appointments, dynastic matters, and emergencies. It does not replace Cabinet or Parliament. The Council of State bridges Crown and government through constitutional review, administrative law, senior appointments, disputes, and emergency continuity. Its unresolved jurisdiction becomes most important when ordinary constitutional sovereignty collides with hidden supernatural authority that the public state cannot formally acknowledge. Narvea retains its own hierarchy of court and civil ranks. Rank determines precedence and status, but does not necessarily describe a person's actual job. A State Councillor might serve as an ambassador, judge, governor, rector, or senior ministry official. Drake holds the rank of State Councillor and the office of Official for Special Assignments. The office makes him an elite executive troubleshooter attached to a high-ranking personal office rather than a routine administrator. He can carry delegated authority into confidential criminal investigations, political counter-espionage, emergency corruption audits, and diplomatic errands. His friendship with the Duke begins when Drake is the only official willing to tell him that he is wrong. That refusal to flatter earns exceptional access and occasional forgiveness, but later makes Drake deeply unpopular at Court, where courtiers deride him as the Duke's pampered favorite. Cultural character Narvea carries layered coastal, inland, courtly, mercantile, urban, rural, and frontier traditions. Catholic and Orthodox communities coexist across regions with distinct architecture, memory, dialect, and politics. The result is not a uniform cultural mixture. The state itself is what connects its different regions. The central tension Narvea lives through a permanent partnership, and occasional rivalry, between inherited continuity and popular government. A modern minister can hold an old civil rank. A national officer can attend a ceremony governed by ducal precedence. An elected Prime Minister controls policy but still travels to the palace for a formal audience. That tension between modern public life and inherited hierarchy is central to the country, and to the story unfolding inside it. Narvean State Archive

entries.title: What Can You Tell Me About Magi?
entries.subtitle: Magistry
entries.text: What Can You Tell Me About Magi? Magistry A dialogue on the nature, secrecy, religion, and politics of Magi. What Can You Tell Me About Magi? Journalist: “What can you tell me about Magi?” Fionn: “That depends on whether you want the answer fit for a child, a priest, or a judge.” Journalist: “The true one.” Fionn: “A dangerous preference.” Fionn: “Very well. Magi do not create miracles. They exploit them.” Journalist: “Explain.” Fionn: “Nature is full of pressure points. Fault lines. Small mercies in the machinery. Most men live their entire lives without seeing them. A Magus sees them, presses where others only endure, and obtains from the world an effect that the world was already willing to permit.” Journalist: “So your craft is natural.” Fionn: “Do not say that too loudly. It upsets both the devout and the educated, though for different reasons.” Journalist: “And the common word for it?” Fionn: “Magic. Superstition. Blasphemy. Treason, on difficult days.” Journalist: “You speak of it with very little reverence.” Fionn: “I was not asked to admire it.” Journalist: “Then what are Magi, truly?” Fionn: “Loopholes. Human ones.” Journalist: “You say that as if it were an accusation.” Fionn: “It often is.” Journalist: “And what follows from this?” Fionn: “What follows is secrecy. Always secrecy. A society can forgive murder more easily than it can forgive a wound in its understanding of nature.” Journalist: “That is a severe claim.” Fionn: “It is also a practical one.” Journalist: “You mean that a witness must die.” Fionn: “I mean that the world protects its coherence with astonishing cruelty.” Journalist: “That was not my question.” Fionn: “No. But it was the truthful answer.” Journalist: “And the Church?” Fionn: “The Church is wiser than statesmen and less honest than philosophers. It knows enough to fear us, enough to use us, and enough to deny both.” Journalist: “And politics?” Fionn: “Politics is forbidden.” Journalist: “Forbidden, or impossible?” Fionn: “Neither. Merely expensive.” Journalist,Fionn

entries.title: The Drowned Chorus
entries.subtitle: HI-003 · Operational encounter
entries.text: The Drowned Chorus HI-003 · Operational encounter HI-003 the-drowned-chorus The Drowned Chorus Operational encounter embodied environmental A pale girl rises from the water with her eyes sewn shut by fishing line and a dress made from dead fish. She speaks with the combined voices of drowned people. An ordinary report cannot reconcile the body, the voices, and the conditions of the encounter. Surviving fragments may be treated as trauma, darkness, waterborne confusion, or mutually reinforced misperception. The figure may be a body assembled by the water, a vessel for accumulated drownings, or the visible portion of a larger river-bound manifestation. The dead are expressed as a chorus through one visible figure. Her appearance binds water, fishing, drowning, and human remains into a single image. No countermeasure is confirmed. Lynleit's blue flame is capable of opposing Holumns that ordinary weapons cannot finish, but the outcome of this encounter remains part of the boat operation. This is the entity encountered during the failed boat operation. It turns the river from a setting into an active part of the Spill. embodied,environmental

entries.title: The Last Piece
entries.subtitle: HI-002 · Missing-person incident
entries.text: The Last Piece HI-002 · Missing-person incident HI-002 the-last-piece The Last Piece Missing-person incident event curse A puzzle purchased at a market compels its owner to finish it. When the final piece is placed, the owner disappears and enters the missing-persons archive. Investigators see a purchased object, a developed obsession, and a disappearance. The puzzle may be treated as an unrelated possession, a clue to voluntary flight, or an instrument used by another person. The compulsion and completion are parts of the same rule. The final piece does not merely precede the disappearance. It completes the condition that permits it. Attention narrows into addiction. Completion is followed by permanent disappearance, while the object remains available to be found again. No countermeasure is confirmed. Refusing completion appears safer than solving the object, but the strength and transfer of the compulsion remain unknown. The incident establishes that a Holumn may be an event encoded into an ordinary object rather than a creature concealed inside it. event,curse

entries.title: The River That Is Too Deep
entries.subtitle: HI-004 · Accumulated incident pattern
entries.text: The River That Is Too Deep HI-004 · Accumulated incident pattern HI-004 the-river-that-is-too-deep The River That Is Too Deep Accumulated incident pattern embodied environmental Something immense moves beneath the city river despite stretches too shallow to contain it. Impossible waves damage boats and kayaks, while drowned bodies lose pieces to bites larger than any expected river predator could make. Each report can be separated into wake damage, submerged debris, boating accidents, postmortem animal activity, or exaggerated witness comparison. Together they remain difficult to explain without inventing a cause the river should not contain. The leviathan may be an animal-like Holumn, the river giving itself predatory mass, or a depth that exists only when the manifestation passes through it. The river behaves as though it can briefly contain a body larger than its physical depth. Water displacement, impact damage, and feeding traces persist after the shape itself is gone. No countermeasure is confirmed. Its dependence on the river may be a boundary, but it is not yet known whether the water contains the Holumn or belongs to it. The pattern supports the possibility that the Spill changes what a place is capable of containing, not only what creatures can enter it. embodied,environmental

entries.title: The Voice on the Line
entries.subtitle: HI-001 · Victim testimony
entries.text: The Voice on the Line HI-001 · Victim testimony HI-001 the-voice-on-the-line The Voice on the Line Victim testimony disembodied curse Have you heard of a telephone call that answers to you in your own voice? At first I thought whoever was on the phone was repeating me. But it was my own voice. At first it felt like an echo, as all it did was repeat my words. But then it started calling me incessantly, and it was talking to me, in bizarre ways. In my own voice. Police and communications specialists would first investigate harassment, recording fraud, a compromised exchange, equipment failure, or a witness in psychological distress. Magi and special envoys treat the change from repetition to unsolicited speech as the decisive detail. Something learned the witness's voice, then began using it without the witness. Imitation develops into initiative. The calls become incessant and the borrowed voice speaks in ways the witness does not recognize as their own thought. No countermeasure is confirmed. The incident establishes that a Holumn can enter ordinary infrastructure and acquire presence without forming a visible body. disembodied,curse

entries.title: A Meeting Beyond Authority
entries.subtitle: MOM-005 · Unknowing Convergence
entries.text: A Meeting Beyond Authority MOM-005 · Unknowing Convergence At night on a hill overlooking Vilen, Sherie leads an illegal negotiation in which Drake seeks limited access to MSF resources without surrendering sensitive evidence. Binds the government and MSF investigations together through an alliance that is politically dangerous before anyone understands that the underlying threat is magical. It is Sherie's first independent diplomatic success, not a transfer of Drake's wider role as the story's primary strategic mind. A hill overlooking Vilen Sherie believes her uncle when the Court does not. Sherie is Drake's niece and is training under him to become a diplomat. The approach to Lynleit is entirely Sherie's idea and strategy. Sherie develops the plan against Drake's wishes, persuades him to participate, and takes charge of the meeting and negotiations. Drake remains opposed to the illegal approach but attends after Sherie overcomes his resistance. After the negotiation succeeds, Sherie asks Drake to praise and pamper her for her first achievement. Drake still cannot decide whether an alliance with Lynleit is a strategic advantage or a dangerous mistake. Drake remains the story's main strategic mind before and after this event. The meeting takes place at night on a hill overlooking Vilen. Drake does not hand sensitive evidence to people outside the aristocratic circle. He and Sherie request access to selected MSF resources and capabilities in exchange for concessions or favors. Sherie and Drake bring Heyk as their bodyguard and confidant. Lynleit brings Felix, Reiner, and Kyrien as her bodyguards and confidants. The main negotiation belongs to Lynleit, Sherie, and a reluctant Drake, while the others contribute opinions and warnings. Lynleit regards the request as dangerous. Felix openly protests, while Kyrien stays silent and tests the suspected conspiracy against his own past grievances. What concessions or favors do Drake and Sherie offer for access to MSF resources? Which precise MSF capabilities do they request, and what operational limits does Lynleit impose? What would finally convince Drake that the alliance should be preserved or abandoned? Sherie must persuade Drake that Lynleit is worth the legal and political danger of contact. Sherie claims praise and pampering for her success while Drake remains uncertain about what she has created. The private agreement then produces a narrow intelligence operation focused on a suspected shipment rather than an arrest or seizure. Drake drake Sherie sherie Lynleit lynleit Felix felix Reiner reiner Kyrien kyrien Heyk heyk

entries.title: After the Failed Attempt
entries.subtitle: MOM-001 · The Hidden Wager
entries.text: After the Failed Attempt MOM-001 · The Hidden Wager Lynleit interrogates Kyrien after his failed attempt to assassinate a Magus politician, then converts his prison risk into a secret recruitment. Creates the coercive bargain that begins Kyrien's hidden association with MSF in the first few chapters. Lynleit accepts the risk because she senses danger approaching before she can prove its shape. The decision also leaves a surviving Magus politician whose later retaliation reaches her. Police office Kyrien has made a failed attempt to assassinate a politician who belongs to the Magi world. The immediate aftermath brings him into a police office. Lynleit conducts the interrogation. Lynleit invokes an extraordinary transfer clause in MSF's government service contract, drafted under Fionn for extraordinary threats. The transfer gives her control of Kyrien's case without requiring her to disclose the secret recruitment to Fionn. Kyrien faces prison unless he agrees to become Lynleit's secret helper. His freedom remains conditional on accepting Lynleit's demands, leaving him confined to her whims. Lynleit's private strategy is to keep Kyrien as a secret trump card against Helena. The recruitment occurs within the first few chapters, well before Fionn's assassination. Lynleit acts because her intuition warns her of near-future danger before she has enough evidence to define it. Lynleit is Fionn's biological daughter. Helena is Lynleit's stepmother and Fionn's wife. Lynleit already suspects Helena of being an enemy despite that family relationship. Kyrien's father held an important position in Narvea's military. The targeted politician was involved in causing his father's death. Kyrien obtained the knowledge and tools for the attempt through his father's military background. The attempt fails solely because the politician belongs to the Magi world. The politician's survival later creates consequences for Lynleit. Lynleit notices Helena probing Fionn's schedules, visitors to the family house, trusted officers, and Lynleit's own travel. Lynleit suspects murder because Helena appears to be studying the family too carefully. What is the politician's name, office, and exact role in Kyrien's father's death? How does the surviving politician later retaliate against Lynleit? What initial cover story conceals Kyrien's release and unofficial MSF association? Kyrien's father's death, the politician's involvement, and the military knowledge behind the attempt still need connective scenes. Kyrien enters Lynleit's service unwillingly. Lynleit must later decide who, if anyone, can be trusted with the secret. The arrangement preserves him as hidden leverage against Helena through the early investigation. Fionn's much later assassination vindicates Lynleit's warning without proving that she understood its source. Lynleit lynleit Kyrien kyrien

entries.title: At the End of the First Arc
entries.subtitle: MOM-012 · Lynleit Disappears
entries.text: At the End of the First Arc MOM-012 · Lynleit Disappears After a story-long accumulation of functional trust and non-sexual intimacy, Lynleit and Kyrien finally have sex at the end of the first arc, shortly before her pregnancy and disappearance. Completes a progression that begins with protected knowledge and shared warmth after the river incident, deepens through emotional refuge after Fionn's murder, and becomes sexual only when the first arc is closing. Unspecified location Lynleit and Kyrien's intimacy develops slowly and functionally across the entire story. The relationship remains non-sexual through the river aftermath and the much later hotel-room refuge. Their relationship becomes sexual at the end of the first arc. The encounter occurs before Lynleit's pregnancy and disappearance. What final circumstances bring them together at the end of the arc? Is this encounter the conception of their son? When does Lynleit realize she is pregnant, and how much time passes before she disappears? The river incident establishes silent physical trust. The hotel-room refuge after Fionn's murder establishes emotional safety. Additional functional encounters must make the final threshold feel accumulated rather than sudden. Lynleit becomes pregnant close to the end of the arc and disappears to keep the child beyond the conflict's reach. Kyrien is left to direct MSF without knowing that she carries their son. Lynleit lynleit Kyrien kyrien

entries.title: Beyond the Cordon
entries.subtitle: MOM-010 · The Quarantine
entries.text: Beyond the Cordon MOM-010 · The Quarantine Hiyu enters the quarantined park to test his impossible suspicion that magic is involved in the disappearances. Yulia goes with him to prove the theory wrong and keep him alive. Places two opposite investigative methods inside the same impossible case: Hiyu's generative intuition reaches the right category without understanding it, while Yulia's disciplined criminology loses the ordinary rules it depends upon. The quarantined park in Vilen Hiyu and Yulia are university students in their mid-twenties who study criminology. Yulia is a classical ISTJ and the top student in their class, with meticulous command of detail and criminological protocol. Hiyu is an ENTP whose personal investigations rely on intuitive threads, improvised methods, and rapid hypothesis generation. Without knowing that magic exists, Hiyu suspects it is involved in the disappearances. Yulia enters partly to prove him wrong and partly to prevent him from facing the danger alone. How do they bypass the cordon? What do they find, and how do they survive or escape? What lasting evidence, injury, or change in their relationship follows the trespass? The widening disappearance case gives Hiyu enough fragments to form an impossible but directionally correct theory. Yulia rejects the conclusion but refuses to let him test it alone. Whatever they witness must connect two civilian students to the larger institutional response without turning Hiyu's correct category into complete knowledge of magic. Hiyu hiyu Yulia yulia

entries.title: Shelter after the Accusation
entries.subtitle: MOM-011 · Clear Her Name
entries.text: Shelter after the Accusation MOM-011 · Clear Her Name After exhausting her available resources to escape the directed hunt for her arrest, Lynleit reaches Kyrien's hotel-room hideout and finally loses the composure that carried her through the immediate crisis. Marks a much later threshold in an intimacy that began functionally after the river incident. Safety, grief, and care turn the coerced alliance into emotional reliance without making the relationship sexual yet. Kyrien's hotel-room hideout Lynleit acts rationally and efficiently during the accusation and escape. Helena's response is a directed hunt for Lynleit's arrest. Lynleit uses every available resource she can reach to evade capture. Her emotions surface only after she reaches safety in Kyrien's hotel room. She stays the night. There is no sexual interaction between them. Kyrien holds her while she falls asleep. The hotel-room refuge occurs much later than the river incident and only after Fionn has been murdered. Their earlier intimate encounters are non-sexual and arise functionally from isolation, danger, cold, near drowning, or emotional rupture. The first trigger is Kyrien's silent protection of Lynleit's water-walking secret and their back-to-back attempt to share body heat after the river incident. Later sexual intimacy is not deliberately pursued. It develops as something emotionally unavoidable. Their relationship becomes sexual at the end of the first arc. The sexual encounter precedes Lynleit's pregnancy and disappearance. How does Lynleit locate the hideout without leading pursuit to Kyrien? What does she say once her composure breaks? What changes between them the following morning? Helena has used Fionn's death to frame Lynleit and direct a hunt for her arrest, forcing her to rely on the secret ally she recruited long before the danger became visible. Their bond remains non-sexual at this point, but it becomes a private source of safety that later intimacy can grow from without feeling sudden or sought for its own sake. Kyrien next helps Lynleit establish contact with Felix and Reiner, beginning her slow campaign to reclaim MSF while she remains hunted. Lynleit lynleit Kyrien kyrien

entries.title: The Boat Beneath the Bridge
entries.subtitle: MOM-006 · Unknowing Convergence
entries.text: The Boat Beneath the Bridge MOM-006 · Unknowing Convergence Lynleit leads an unsanctioned nighttime infiltration of a passing boat. The intelligence-only raid collapses into a supernatural calamity and forces her to use her secret ability to walk on water in combat for the first time. Turns a political conspiracy investigation into the first direct proof that Magi are involved, exposes Lynleit's most forbidden talent under conditions she cannot fully control, and creates the first trigger in her slowly developing intimacy with Kyrien. Unspecified bridge and river The MSF team is ordered to enter and leave unseen, gathering intelligence without stopping the suspected transfer. The officers descend by rope from a bridge onto a boat passing beneath them after nightfall. The operation goes badly enough that the operatives must swim ashore on their own. The others do not immediately realize that Lynleit has been left to face a supernatural calamity. Lynleit recognizes that the plot is not solely political and that Magi are involved. The crisis becomes the first combat test of her ability to walk on water. Only Kyrien witnesses Lynleit walking on water. Kyrien is too careful to acknowledge what he saw and feigns innocence convincingly. They reach the night park drenched and struggling to catch their breath. They sit with their backs pressed together to share body heat while they recover. Lynleit indirectly asks whether Kyrien saw anything strange during the escape. Kyrien denies seeing anything, and his careful performance of innocence gives Lynleit nothing she can safely test. This act of unspoken protection becomes the first trigger in an intimacy that develops slowly and functionally across the story. The encounter leaves a supernatural scar in the river rather than only a surviving creature. What form does the river's scar take, and in what sense does the place remember the encounter? Which additional MSF officers join the infiltration? What intelligence survives the failed operation? The covert meeting must identify the boat and establish why observation is safer than interception. Drenched and seated back to back in the night park, Lynleit and Kyrien preserve a mutual silence around what he witnessed. The shared warmth and his refusal to expose her establish physical trust without romance being stated or pursued. Much later, after Fionn's murder, the hotel-room refuge deepens that trust into emotional reliance. Lynleit lynleit Felix felix Kyrien kyrien

entries.title: The Cat in the Family House
entries.subtitle: MOM-002 · Vanishing Point
entries.text: The Cat in the Family House MOM-002 · Vanishing Point Before the crisis reaches her home directly, Lynleit clumsily chases a grey cat that has trespassed into the family house, catches it, then cannot bring herself to expel it into the rain. Shows Lynleit's clumsy and childish private side while using the grey intruder as an omen. Outside threats and tragedies have begun to bleed into her life, and the escaping cat becomes an emotional symbol for her slipping leads, understanding, and sense of safety. The Director's House The scene occurs in the early chapters, after danger has begun outside but before Lynleit's life starts to collapse. A grey cat trespasses into Lynleit's family house and becomes an omen of outside threats entering her private life. The family maintained an original house in Turon while Lynleit's mother was alive and Lynleit was in junior school. After her mother's death, the family moved to a Vilen residence for Fionn's access to the capital. Lynleit accepted the move only after securing the third-floor study-bedroom. The Vilen house is a three-floor family residence on a wooded hill above the river that flows toward the city center, with a small rear park and garden. Lynleit values the thick vegetation and the sound of leaves and branches in the wind. She regards nearby flowing water as life energy and seeks its emotional grounding despite her childhood fear of drowning. The garden-facing first floor contains glass-enclosed relaxation areas that preserve contact with nature through every season. Lynleit personally chases the cat through the house, revealing a clumsier and more childish side of her than her public role usually permits. As the cat repeatedly escapes her, Lynleit intuitively and emotionally connects it with her leads, understanding of her life, and sense of safety escaping her control. Lynleit eventually catches the cat. She cannot bring herself to expel it because rain is falling outside. The cat decides to remain and becomes a permanent loiterer in the family home. Does the cat ever receive a name? Who else in the household accepts or resists its permanent presence? The first disappearances have begun outside Lynleit's private life, but the full crisis, Fionn's death, and the destruction of her family security remain ahead. The cat remains inside the house as a quiet domestic echo of the danger Lynleit cannot keep outside. Later losses can turn the once-comic chase into an omen whose meaning becomes clear only in retrospect. Lynleit lynleit

entries.title: The First Lines Back into MSF
entries.subtitle: MOM-013 · Clear Her Name
entries.text: The First Lines Back into MSF MOM-013 · Clear Her Name While Lynleit remains the target of an active arrest hunt, Kyrien helps her find secure ways to contact Felix and Reiner. Their reconnection becomes the first step in her slow campaign to reclaim MSF from Helena. Bridges Lynleit's immediate escape and hotel refuge to an organized counteroffensive. The hidden ally Helena did not know becomes the route back to the two trusted officers she does know. Unspecified secure contact points Lynleit remains actively hunted for arrest after escaping the immediate accusation. Kyrien helps her find ways to contact Felix and Reiner without surrendering her location. Felix and Reiner are the first trusted MSF officers brought back into her fugitive network. The renewed contact begins Lynleit's slow effort to reclaim MSF from Helena. The counteroffensive develops while Lynleit remains hunted rather than after the danger has passed. What secure method does Kyrien use to reach Felix and Reiner? Which officer responds first, and how does Lynleit prove the contact is genuine? What first foothold inside MSF can Felix and Reiner give her without exposing themselves? Which arresting authorities and MSF units are actively searching for Lynleit at this point? Lynleit reaches Kyrien's hotel room after exhausting her immediate escape resources, and his refuge becomes the only stable point in her flight. The four-person link gives Lynleit an internal line into Helena's MSF and begins a prolonged contest for legitimacy, intelligence, and control under the pressure of an active manhunt. Lynleit lynleit Kyrien kyrien Felix felix Reiner reiner

entries.title: The First Missing Man
entries.subtitle: MOM-003 · Vanishing Point
entries.text: The First Missing Man MOM-003 · Vanishing Point The first man to disappear appears to be the Spill's first victim, but he independently causes the crisis. His identity and significance remain concealed for most of the story while hidden factions begin exploiting the catastrophe he created. Makes the apparent first victim the buried cause of an independent crisis, allowing a later identity revelation to reframe both the Holumn disappearances and the agendas built around them. Vilen park, exact site unspecified The first missing person is a man. He is the person who causes the Spill. His identity and significance are not revealed for most of the story. He initially appears to be a victim rather than the originator of the crisis. The Spill begins as an independent crisis rather than an operation created by the hidden conspiracy. Other factions recognize and exploit the crisis for their own purposes. The later disappearances are caused by Holumns. Who is the man? How does he cause the Spill? Why does his identity become pivotal later? Which faction first recognizes and exploits what he caused? Who notices his disappearance first? His public identity and ordinary routine must conceal the significance he will acquire later. Holumns begin taking further victims, while the first disappearance is treated as the start of the case rather than its concealed cause.

entries.title: The Last Man out of the Park
entries.subtitle: MOM-009 · The Quarantine
entries.text: The Last Man out of the Park MOM-009 · The Quarantine A specially equipped paramilitary unit enters the sealed park and is massacred by forces it cannot understand. Captain Heyk becomes the sole survivor. Turns a public missing-person crisis into a state-level containment failure and gives Heyk the grief, access, and personal motive that carry him into Drake and Sherie's service. The quarantined park in Vilen The park quarantine follows the disappearances of citizens, private investigators, and police officers. Police enforce the first closure before the park is sealed even from them. The government deploys specially equipped paramilitary units to investigate the whole park. The unit commanded by Captain Heyk is massacred by forces he cannot understand or explain. Heyk is the sole survivor. The Ducal Guard evacuates him briefly under Drake's orders. He is subsequently recruited into the Ducal Guard as a field agent and bodyguard serving Drake and Sherie's interests. His continuing motive is grief for the squad he lost. What does Heyk perceive during the massacre, and which parts of his account can he articulate? Why does Drake have enough warning or access to order the Ducal Guard evacuation? What evidence, equipment, or injury leaves the park with Heyk? The public already knows that people are missing. Gas, poison, or another harmful substance remains a possible explanation, although no bodies have been recovered. Heyk enters Drake and Sherie's orbit carrying grief, survivor knowledge, and direct experience that no official material explanation can fully contain. Heyk heyk Drake drake Sherie sherie

entries.title: The Secret Third Ally
entries.subtitle: MOM-008 · The Hidden Wager
entries.text: The Secret Third Ally MOM-008 · The Hidden Wager Lynleit eventually tells only Felix and Reiner that she has recruited Kyrien as an unknown ally and possible trump card against Helena, keeping the decision hidden even from Fionn. Defines Lynleit's first deeply anti-protocol MSF decision early in the story, turns secrecy into an advantage over Helena, and establishes the split between Reiner's trust in Lynleit's judgment and Felix's lasting distrust of Kyrien. Unspecified location Helena knows everyone already inside Lynleit's circle, so an unknown ally creates a favorable information imbalance. Felix and Reiner are already Lynleit's close, long-standing friends before the story begins, not subordinates who become her friends during this crisis. Lynleit eventually confines Kyrien's recruitment to Felix and Reiner and does not inform even Fionn. This is Lynleit's first deeply anti-protocol MSF decision, made with strong intuitive conviction. Fionn's assassination is still far ahead when the compartment is created. The later assassination validates Lynleit's sense of approaching danger, although it does not prove she foresaw the event itself. Felix and Reiner both regard Kyrien as a possible threat to Lynleit, especially when neither bodyguard is near her. Reiner accepts the arrangement because he chooses to trust Lynleit's judgment. Felix accepts only after Reiner's decision leaves him in the minority. Felix never fully learns to trust Kyrien and later clashes with him repeatedly. Lynleit reprimands Felix when those clashes interfere with her decision or the arrangement around Kyrien. Where and when does Lynleit disclose the compartment to Felix and Reiner? What evidence or argument does Lynleit use to justify trusting Kyrien? What continuing cover story protects the compartment from Fionn, Helena, the police, and the wider MSF? Which clash between Felix and Kyrien produces the most serious consequence for Lynleit or an operation? What would Fionn do if he learned Lynleit had hidden Kyrien from him? Lynleit has already coerced Kyrien into service after the failed assassination attempt, but the arrangement initially exists only between handler and asset. Reiner becomes the stabilizing vote that permits the compartment to continue. Felix complies without trust, creating recurring friction with Kyrien and forcing Lynleit to defend the judgment on which the entire imbalance depends. Lynleit lynleit Kyrien kyrien Felix felix Reiner reiner

entries.title: The Unresolved Assassination
entries.subtitle: MOM-007 · The Takeover
entries.text: The Unresolved Assassination MOM-007 · The Takeover Fionn is assassinated when several incompatible agendas converge without one actor controlling the whole outcome. Helena knowingly opens one part of the path, then uses his death to seize MSF and frame Lynleit. Preserves Fionn's death as the hinge between hidden conflict and visible takeover while making the unresolved mystery a collision of motives, partial knowledge, and accidental cooperation rather than one clean chain of command. Unspecified location Fionn is successfully assassinated. His death creates the opening Helena uses to take control of MSF. Helena frames Lynleit for the assassination and directs a hunt for her arrest. Helena knowingly enables one part of the pressure against Fionn without understanding everything that follows. No single participant controls the complete assassination outcome. Several incompatible agendas accidentally cooperate to produce Fionn's death. The broader conflict already includes pressure from criminal Magi, foreign Magiarchates, and church actors. The unresolved issue is how each participant's intended outcome and partial action converge into the assassination. What outcome do the criminal Magi seek around Fionn? What separate outcome does a rival foreign Magiarchate seek? What separate outcome does a church faction seek? Which actions accidentally cooperate even though their authors do not share one objective? Did one faction covertly or illegally infiltrate another and use its people or resources without authorization? Does any participant's apparent affiliation conceal who truly directed them? Which door does Helena knowingly open, what does she expect to happen, and what follows beyond her knowledge? Manufactured political strife isolates Fionn and divides his attention while the Spill develops. Helena converts the vacancy into control of MSF, makes Lynleit the official suspect, and directs a hunt for her arrest while the true authorship remains hidden. Fionn fionn Helena helena

entries.text: The Warning Dismissed MOM-004 · Unknowing Convergence State Councillor Drake becomes convinced that a coup is developing somewhere inside Narvea, but neither his peers nor the Duke believe he has found more than disconnected irregularities. Establishes the political explanation that first draws government figures toward the disappearances. Court resentment over Drake's friendship with the Duke deepens his isolation until an illegal alliance feels necessary. Ducal Court Drake is deeply convinced that a coup is underway. Drake holds the rank of State Councillor and has an unusually close personal relationship with the Duke. Their friendship begins when Drake is the only official willing to tell the Duke that the Duke is wrong. The Duke openly refers to Drake as a close friend and sometimes forgives his mistakes. Courtiers shun Drake as the Duke's pampered favorite and overlook that he originally earned the relationship by refusing to flatter him. He cannot yet identify where the conspiracy begins or how far it reaches. His peers ridicule the suspicion and the Duke remains skeptical. Drake interprets the park disappearances as possible cover for the illegal movement of material intended for action against Narvea or Ducal authority. The apparent coup is a political mask over a deeper conflict involving Fionn, Magiarchs abroad, and manipulative actors across several churches. What first convinces Drake that the irregularities form a coup attempt? Which peers lead the ridicule at Court? Is somebody deliberately encouraging the Court to dismiss him? Which criminal Magi, foreign Magiarchates, and church actors are shaping the conspiracy from outside Drake's field of view? Early disappearances and irregular movements need to produce the evidence that Drake reads as one political pattern. Sherie responds to her uncle's isolation by proposing contact with Lynleit outside every lawful chain of supervision. Drake drake

entries.title: Ren L17 “Sparrow”
entries.subtitle: Compact institutional and concealed-carry sidearm
entries.text: Ren L17 “Sparrow” Compact institutional and concealed-carry sidearm Ren L17 Sparrow 9×17 mm / .380 ACP Compact institutional and concealed-carry sidearm Small, discreet, elegant institutional pistol Standard-issued pistol for every MSF officer who has passed weapons certification. MSF purchases the Sparrow from Ren Arms and does not manufacture firearms. A slim, compact, silver-finished pistol with an elegant and deliberately understated appearance. Its proportions sit conceptually between the Walther PPK and SIG Sauer P230, slightly more elongated and graceful than a PPK while retaining enough visual weight to avoid looking fragile. Narrow silver slide Gently rounded upper profile Exposed hammer and small conventional sights Dark grip panels contrasting with silver metal Smooth exterior surfaces and restrained controls Designed for personnel who carry it far more often than they fire it Despite the Sparrow's older design lineage, current-production models omit an external manual safety to reflect the demands and handling priorities of modern combat. The silver finish belongs to the firearm itself rather than to an MSF customization. Routine issue gradually makes the ordinary Ren Arms product visually associated with MSF officers. Its small size, light visual presence, discretion, and modest chambering. lynleit Lynleit Carries the issued Sparrow as her personal sidearm. Walther PPK SIG Sauer P230 Ren Arms Rennel, Narvea

entries.title: Ren L19 “Magpie”
entries.subtitle: Heavier compact service pistol
entries.text: Ren L19 “Magpie” Heavier compact service pistol Ren L19 Magpie 9×19 mm Heavier compact service pistol Larger, louder, and heavier relative of the Sparrow An enlarged and strengthened development of the Sparrow for the more powerful 9×19 cartridge. It retains the older Ren Arms family line while becoming thicker, heavier, visually denser, and more assertive. Graceful slide profile and exposed hammer Narrow forward profile Restrained controls Recognizably Ren Arms grip and frame lines Metallic finishes remain common Darker service finishes may exist Despite the Magpie's older design lineage, current-production models omit an external manual safety to reflect the demands and handling priorities of modern combat. Two optional attachments help the compact pistol remain controllable under the stronger recoil of its 9×19 cartridge. Attachable compensator Reduces muzzle rise and helps the shooter maintain control under the Magpie's greater recoil. Extended magazine Adds gripping surface for firmer recoil control while also increasing ammunition capacity. It fills the space between a discreet institutional pistol and a full modern duty handgun. Its close relationship to the Sparrow, with a larger, louder, heavier, and more noticeable character. entries.title: Holumns
entries.subtitle: Manifestations, effects, and evidence
entries.text: Holumns Manifestations, effects, and evidence Holumn is a category of manifestation, not a biological species. A Holumn may be a physical creature, a natural phenomenon, a repeating event, a disembodied will, or a curse. Its shape follows the fear, memory, fixation, or psychic fracture that gives it pressure. No universal weakness exists. A useful countermeasure must answer the rule expressed by the manifestation. An incident may reveal an effect without revealing the whole Holumn behind it. embodied Embodied A creature or body that occupies physical space, including forms that move without being alive. HI-003 HI-004 environmental Environmental Weather, water, terrain, or another natural system becomes the body or behavior of the manifestation. HI-003 HI-004 event Event-bound The Holumn exists as a sequence, compulsion, rule, or occurrence rather than as a creature that can be confronted directly. HI-002 disembodied Disembodied A voice, memory, desire, or will acquires agency without a stable body of its own. HI-001 curse Curse-bound A person, object, place, or action carries a hostile rule that persists until its particular condition is interrupted. HI-001 HI-002

entries.title: MSF
entries.text: MSF # msf Institutional record Known facts only World / MSF MSF Private intelligence contractor One agency, two purposes MSF is a fully private intelligence business that sells its services to the government. The initials are used publicly without a formal expansion. Fionn built a second purpose beneath its contracted work, preparing mostly ordinary people to approach threats they were never told existed. Legal status Fully private business Primary client Narvean government Headquarters Turon Full name Deliberately unrevealed 01 Dual mandate What members see depends on where they stand CONTRACTED FUNCTION Government services MSF sells intelligence, investigation, security, and operational services to the government while remaining institutionally private. FOUNDER'S DESIGN Contingency structure Fionn quietly shaped MSF so it could confront magical crises. Most members were not told that this purpose, or magic itself, existed. PERMANENT CONVERGENCE Two threat domains The Spill is never fully contained. MSF must shrink into a mainly Magi-focused task force while continuing to handle the ordinary intelligence threats it was created to confront. 02 Ownership and control The government buys access, not ownership PRIVATE GOVERNANCE Its client cannot run the company The government can negotiate contracts, purchase defined services, and decide whether to keep buying them. It has little authority over MSF's succession, command culture, internal appointments, or ordinary workings beyond the access MSF chooses to permit. MSF may also accept clients beyond the government, exposing the danger of a private contract whose obligations conflict with Narvea's interests. Government power Contract, payment, and requested scope MSF control Clients, succession, personnel, command, and internal rules POLITICAL NICKNAME “A legal mafia.” Politically savvy citizens use the joke because MSF combines private loyalty, public contracts, internal succession, and enough concentrated force to make the state uneasy, all while operating within the law. RESIDENTIAL NODE The Director's House Fionn's family residence also supports selected MSF work through its offices and library, while the formal headquarters remains in Turon. → STANDARD SIDEARM Ren L17 "Sparrow" Every MSF officer who passes weapons certification is issued the compact 9×17 pistol. MSF purchases it from Ren Arms rather than manufacturing weapons. → 03 Cryptology in plain sight Authority is worn in blue MSF · B01 ENCRYPTED M.O. A visible signal that looks ordinary Fionn built cryptology into everyday appearance. A deliberate blue garment initiates recognition, but it does not authenticate authority by itself. Top officers follow it with an innocuous challenge-response hidden inside ordinary conversation. Anyone can buy a blue coat. Only someone trusted by Fionn knows how to answer a question that sounds like small talk. Initiation Blue clothing Verification Conversational challenge-response Audience Top officers trusted by Fionn Origin Fionn's private protocol KNOWN USER Lynleit Her blue coat or jacket initiates Fionn's recognition sequence rather than merely expressing a color preference. Even while she is accused and hunted, she can complete the private exchange known to officers he personally trusted. Open Lynleit's profile → LEGITIMACY FAILURE Helena Fionn's most conservative old officers notice Helena's ignorance first. The people least inclined toward rebellion begin questioning her because strict obedience to the founder's protocol now requires disobedience toward his official successor. Open Helena's profile → 04 Command succession Fionn protects every heir by naming none MSF is a private family enterprise, so its succession is an internal struggle rather than a government appointment. Fionn deliberately refuses to identify one uncontested successor because he believes a declared heir would become an obvious target. The government has little standing to settle the vacancy, and his security measure produces the exact succession crisis it was intended to prevent. 01 Fionn Founder without a declared heir Distributes trust through private protocols and overlapping circles, but refuses to turn any one candidate into a visible target. 02 Helena Contested inheritance Takes control after Fionn's elimination and frames Lynleit for his death. Her ignorance of his private authority protocol gradually gives influential officers reason to doubt the legitimacy of her succession. 03 Lynleit Restoration and contraction Fights to clear her name and reclaim the agency. Because the Spill cannot be fully contained, she reshapes MSF into a smaller task force centered on Magi while preserving its intelligence function. 04 Kyrien Non-Magus director Inherits the organization after Lynleit disappears and survives by fully developing MSF's intelligence, evasion, and operational side. 05 Political footprint Turon contains more than a headquarters MSF's concentration of officers in Turon is sufficient to make a small rebellion or secession imaginable. Officer culture, divided logistics, constitutional loyalty, and the absence of any desire to rebel keep that capacity dormant. Politicians remain uneasy because the state cannot simply command or reorganize its private contractor. The final safeguard is the belief that MSF officers are decent people. See Turon in The Duchy → 06 Operational pairing A knight opens angles. A rook holds the line. ♞ KNIGHT PATTERN Felix Hacking and communications let Felix move through an operation indirectly. He finds unexpected access, redirects information, and reaches positions that a straightforward approach cannot. Open Felix's profile → ♜ ROOK PATTERN Reiner Reiner is the physically imposing brute-force specialist. He anchors protection, takes the direct route, and provides controlled power when a line must be held or broken. Open Reiner's profile → 07 Known personnel People who define the institution Founder Fionn Heir and director Lynleit Successor and rival Helena Unofficial asset, later director Kyrien Hacking and communications Felix Brute force and protection Reiner ✎ Page notes MSF Use notes to refine the agency without turning open questions into canon.

entries.title: The Church
entries.text: The Church # the-church Institutional record Known facts only World / The Church † Religious institution Knowledge kept behind doctrine Every church knows about the Magi at the highest point of its hierarchy. That knowledge descends only through controlled channels, leaving most clergy and church staff inside the same protected ignorance as the public. Public role Faith and authority Awareness Every church head Covert arm Special envoys Clergy access Highly restricted 01 Distributed knowledge The institution does not know as one body 01 MAJORITY OF THE CHURCH Ordinary faith Most clergy, staff, and worshippers operate inside the same protected ignorance as the wider public. Religious office alone does not grant access to magical knowledge. 02 HEAD OF THE HIERARCHY Guaranteed awareness The head of every church is aware of the Magi and the concealed world surrounding them. This is the stable point from which each church controls its response. 03 CONTROLLED OPERATORS Special envoys Each church maintains a contingent of operatives who carry the title of special envoy and act in the name of its head. 02 Special envoys Priesthood is the cover, not the profession OFFICIAL APPEARANCE Envoys of the heads of churches Special envoys are trained and presented as priests, allowing them to move through religious institutions with a credible public identity. Their primary preparation is operational rather than pastoral. Authority Act for a church head Cover Priesthood Structure Contingent within each church 01 Politics Institutional access, negotiation, leverage, and influence. 02 Espionage Covert placement, observation, clandestine activity, and the possible penetration of rival institutions. 03 Intelligence Collection, assessment, and controlled circulation of knowledge. 04 Combat Operational force when diplomacy and concealment fail. 05 Assassination A capability held by some envoys, not a universal assignment. 06 Specialization Each envoy develops one or several domains rather than mastering every field. Separate traditions Shared purpose does not mean shared doctrine. Both traditions maintain covert, assassination-capable priesthoods while regarding the other's system as dangerously unaccountable. ORTHODOX CHURCH Trust before procedure Orthodox envoys favor personal chains of trust, confession-like secrecy, and discretionary judgment. Authority moves through relationships whose moral burden rests heavily on the person exercising it. CATHOLIC CHURCH Procedure before discretion Catholic envoys favor dossiers, compartmentalized offices, and codified authorization. Authority moves through records and separated functions intended to prevent any one operative from holding the whole design. PLAUSIBLE, NOT CONFIRMED Special-envoy capabilities make covert or illegal infiltration of Magiarchates and other factions possible. The same risk also runs in reverse, because church structures may themselves be penetrated. 03 Institutional relations Every relationship is conditional WITH THE PUBLIC Protect ignorance Magic remains outside ordinary understanding, and Church knowledge is kept narrow. WITH THE MAGIARCHY Sanction, constrain, and verify Cross-national church structures face Magiarchates that are kept territorial and separate. Both sides hunt unsanctioned Magi, but the Church often doubts that Magiarchs will act decisively enough. WITH THE STATE Reveal only what is necessary Negotiations can occur near public institutions without making their magical subject visible to ordinary officials or officers. WITH RENEGADE MAGI Hunt through special envoys Magi without a jurisdiction who practice outside church supervision or permission are treated as criminals. Special envoys pursue them alongside the resources of the responsible Magiarch. 04 Accepted boundaries Not every possible act is permitted FORBIDDEN MIRACLE-MAKING Harmless effect, prohibited form The Church distinguishes pressure-based magecraft from miracle-making that resembles wizardry or imitates acts associated with Jesus, saints, saviours, and other sacred figures. Walking on water crosses that symbolic boundary. Lynleit conceals the accidental talent because exposure would bring strong punishment even if she had harmed nobody. Open Lynleit's profile → 05 Canon doctrine Suppression doctrine THE PRACTICAL RULE Protect the boundary of public knowledge Suppression doctrine is a shared responsibility of the Church and the Magiarchy for keeping witnesses of magic from carrying dangerous knowledge back into ordinary society. The Church holds final sanction over the doctrine, while Magiarchal resources may investigate, contain, absorb, or remove witnesses under that authority. It is not one fixed punishment. The response depends on what the witness knows, how credible they are, how much exposure has already occurred, and whether the witness can be contained without creating a larger crisis. 01 · IRREVERSIBLE Elimination Murder, assassination, or kidnapping may be considered when the Church believes exposure cannot be contained by other means. 02 · PRESSURE Coercion Extortion, intimidation, bribery, and threats can redirect a witness without making the magical truth public. 03 · REFRAME Discrediting A witness may be framed as mentally ill, unreliable, or otherwise incapable of persuading anyone who hears the account. 04 · ABSORPTION Church integration Some witnesses are forced into Church staff or clergy, where their access, movement, and story can be controlled from inside the institution. 05 · SERVICE Magiarchal integration Others may be absorbed into Magiarchy service staff or a supervised operational role, turning dangerous knowledge into a controlled obligation under Church-sanctioned authority. UNRESOLVED BOUNDARY The doctrine can preserve civilization while also making murder administratively thinkable. The story's open question is where containment ends and institutional killing begins. 06 Story contact The first negotiation is visible only from outside Early in September, Fionn and Lynleit enter a church for negotiations while Felix and Reiner remain outside. They are not merely assigned officers: both are Lynleit's friends and personal bodyguards trusted by Fionn. Even they are denied entry. The subject is kept confidential from them, while Lynleit's early, irritated exit suggests that something important happened inside. Father Mikhail is confirmed as a special envoy, although his specialization and authority in this or later Church operations remain open. Open Story → Meet Father Mikhail → ✎ Page notes The Church Use notes to define doctrine, hierarchy, and boundaries without treating open questions as facts.

entries.title: The Director's House
entries.text: The Director's House # director-house Residential location record Family home · discreet MSF node World / The Director's House Residence · family seat · operational node A family home with institutional gravity The family keeps two houses. The original stands in Turon, where Lynleit lived with her mother during junior school. After her mother's death, Fionn moved the family to Vilen for better access to the capital. The Vilen house is a three-floor residence whose offices, library, and discreet working rooms also support MSF operations. Floors Three Family houses Turon and Vilen Setting Vilen hillside above the river Rear grounds Small park and garden Operational role Residential mini-HQ 01 Family history Two houses, one family history Distant city House on the hill Rear garden City river Behind the house, a compact private park descends toward the river-facing edge of the hill. Thick vegetation and mature trees surround the residence closely enough for wind in the leaves and branches to remain part of its daily sound. Below, the river flows toward Vilen's city center. Lynleit regards flowing water as life energy: its movement gives her emotional grounding even though she has feared drowning since childhood. 02 Vertical plan Three floors, three degrees of distance 03 Highest floor Lynleit's chosen room A desk between trees and water After the family moved from Turon to Vilen, Lynleit made a third-floor study-bedroom her condition for accepting the new house. Its height lets her look beyond the trees toward the river while she works. Wind moving through leaves and branches gives the room the natural sound she finds most inspiring. 02 Private interior Family domain The quieter center of the house The second floor belongs to the residence's private interior. Its precise room plan is not yet fixed, preserving space for family rooms and the boundaries between household life and the work conducted elsewhere in the building. 01 Garden level Glass and greenery Nature without surrendering shelter The rear side of the first floor opens into glass-enclosed relaxation areas facing dense greenery. In summer they extend domestic life among the trees. In winter the same rooms preserve the sight and sound of the landscape while protecting everyone inside from cold, rain, and wind. READING Library A substantial domestic library supports study, research, and the quieter habits of a family whose private responsibilities extend beyond the household. WORK Several offices Multiple offices allow private meetings and administrative work to occur without converting the entire residence into an overt agency building. OPEN DETAIL Exact allocation The floor-by-floor placement of the library, offices, service rooms, and other bedrooms remains intentionally undefined. 03 Dual role Residence and command space occupy the same address FAMILY NEST A place that belongs to the family first Bedrooms, study, reading, the garden, and the glass relaxation rooms give the house a genuine domestic identity. It stores ordinary memories alongside the pressures attached to Fionn's position. SHARED THRESHOLD Privacy becomes operational access The director can receive trusted people, review sensitive work, and continue agency business without leaving the protection and familiarity of home. MINI-HQ A discreet extension of MSF The offices and library let the residence support selected meetings, planning, and confidential work. It complements MSF's formal headquarters in Turon rather than replacing it. 04 Story connections Private rooms become narrative pressure points RESIDENT Lynleit Her third-floor room brings together the distant view, surrounding trees, and flowing water she uses for inspiration and emotional grounding. → DIRECTOR Fionn His public family seat also supports the confidential demands of MSF leadership. → INSTITUTION MSF The house is a residential operational node, distinct from the agency's formal headquarters in Turon. → EARLY OMEN The grey cat An intruder turns the protected family interior into a comic warning that outside danger has begun to enter. → ✎ Page notes House Use notes to refine rooms, access, and domestic details without turning open architecture into canon.

entries.title: The Duchy
entries.text: The Duchy # narvea National reference record Country profile World / The Duchy of Narvea COUNTRY RECORD NAR · 001 Primary setting The Duchy of Narvea A large, sovereign Baltic country built around two sources of legitimacy: the Ducal Crown and the parliamentary state. Sovereignty resides jointly in the Crown and the Nation. Government Constitutional duchy State identity Multinational and civic Parliamentary capital Vilen Ducal seat Rennel MSF headquarters Turon Region Eastern Baltic Story role Main country Diplomatic role European meeting ground Jump to Territory Cities Authority Diplomacy Institutions Culture 01 Territory A state along the eastern Baltic Narvea reaches from the approaches to St. Petersburg toward the southwestern Baltic frontier near Gdansk. National flag Ducal standard Show details for Rennel Show details for Turon Show details for Bird's Nest Show details for Port City Show details for Vilen Map of Narvea Hover, focus, tap, or select a city Mapped roles Why these cities matter Five centers divide Narvea's political, diplomatic, and strategic life. 01 Rennel · Ducal seat Home of the Crown, Court, ceremony, and dynastic archives. It represents continuity and sovereign legitimacy. 02 Turon · MSF headquarters The private contractor's concentration of officers gives it unusual local power. Constitutional loyalty and divided logistics restrain it, but politicians know the final safeguard is the officers' own decency. 03 Bird's Nest · Diplomatic ground Rival nations meet here to negotiate. Every country uses a different name for the city. 04 Port City · Western gateway Narvea's principal western connection to Baltic trade, maritime movement, and foreign access. 05 Vilen · Parliamentary capital Parliament, Cabinet, ministries, courts, and financial institutions make it the center of the modern state. 02 Dual capital tradition One country, two political worlds Rennel carries the memory of the dynasty. Vilen runs the modern state. Turon holds an unspoken political pressure point. Rennel City image placeholder THE CROWN Ducal capital Rennel Located in the old Narva region. It represents dynasty, continuity, military tradition, nobility, and ceremony. Ducal Palace and Court Privy Council Ducal Guard headquarters Dynastic and heraldic archives Formal audiences Vilen City image placeholder THE STATE Parliamentary capital Vilen Narvea's center of government, law, administration, commerce, and modern political life. Its enormous urban park becomes the first visible center of the disappearances. Parliament and Cabinet Government ministries Major courts Financial institutions Vast park at the center of the first disappearances Turon City image placeholder THE PRESSURE POINT MSF headquarters Turon Turon is home to the headquarters of MSF, a fully private intelligence business that sells services to the government while retaining control of its own succession and internal affairs. Its officers give the company enough local force to mount a small rebellion or attempt secession if it ever chose to do so. Officer culture, divided logistics, constitutional loyalty, and a genuine lack of separatist ambition keep that possibility theoretical. MSF headquarters and senior officer corps Operational strength beyond ordinary agency needs Potential leverage over the central government Political anxiety that ultimately depends on personal restraint No rebellion is openly planned. The possibility simply remains in the backrooms of Narvean political life, where senior officials cannot afford to ignore it. 03 Constitutional balance Parliament governs. The Crown safeguards. Parliament chooses and controls the government, passes laws, and authorizes public money. The Duke gives constitutional form to those decisions and intervenes only through narrowly defined reserve powers. C Ducal sphere The Duke Head of state and constitutional guardian. Formally appoints the Prime Minister who commands parliamentary confidence Promulgates laws already passed by Parliament without rewriting them Represents the state, receives ambassadors, and maintains the Court and Ducal Guard Uses narrow reserve powers only during constitutional emergencies CROWN CONSTITUTIONAL BALANCE NATION P Democratic sphere Parliament & Government Elected authority and the executive accountable to it. Parliament grants or withdraws confidence in the Prime Minister and government Parliament debates, amends, and passes laws and approves taxation and spending The Prime Minister directs Cabinet, ministries, and the civil service The government sets domestic, defence, economic, social, and ordinary foreign policy 04 Diplomatic tradition The room where Europe stepped back Narvea became a trusted meeting ground where opposing European powers could settle their differences before rivalry became open conflict. NEUTRAL GROUND Authority meets here before force. Narvea's influence rests less on commanding Europe than on keeping its rivals in the same room long enough to avoid escalation. Method Conference and settlement Legacy Borders shaped without continental war 1803 to 1815 NAPOLEONIC WARS Narvea helped contain a continental crisis Its mediation played an important and constructive role during the wars. The settlements of this period also began shaping Narvea's borders into their modern form. 1917 EASTERN SETTLEMENT Revolution was prevented Opposing powers gathered in Narvea and contained an eastern political crisis before it could become a revolution. 1939 CONTINENTAL SETTLEMENT Europe avoided a major war Another Narvean conference stopped escalation between European powers, allowing the continent's borders and history to take a different course. NOW LIVING LEGACY Diplomacy became ordinary culture The habit of mediation still shapes how Narvean institutions understand authority, legitimacy, and public service. LANGUAGE AS CIVIC PRACTICE Multilingualism is expected, not exceptional. People in authority are expected to know several languages, but the custom reaches far beyond diplomatic circles. Narveans often move between languages in ordinary conversation for precision, courtesy, emphasis, or simple habit, even when no negotiation is taking place. THE CITY WITH MANY NAMES Bird's Nest is only one of its titles. Most negotiations between rival nations take place in this city. Every country calls it something different, carrying its own name for the same diplomatic ground. Bird's Nest is the Narvean title, and its unusual sound reflects the city's role as the place where competing powers gather without fully belonging to one another. 05 Institutions Parallel systems, one state Responsibility is divided deliberately. Similar-looking institutions can answer to different centers of authority. STATE · 01 Narvean Armed Forces The national Army, Navy, Air Force, reserves, and intelligence services answer through the constitutional government. National defence CROWN · 01 Ducal Guard An elite Crown formation protecting the ducal family, residences, and selected constitutional institutions. Dynastic security STATE · 02 Narvean Police Ordinary law enforcement remains under civilian authority, most likely through the Ministry of the Interior. Public order CROWN · 02 Privy Council Advises the Duke on constitutional questions, appointments, security, foreign affairs, and emergencies. Sovereign counsel BRIDGE · 01 Council of State A standing bridge between Crown and government for constitutional review, administrative law, major appointments, disputes, and emergency continuity. Its most dangerous cases begin when ordinary state sovereignty collides with supernatural authority the public constitution cannot acknowledge. Jurisdictional paradox Service and precedence Rank is not the same as office Narvea maintains its own hierarchy of court and civil ranks. A person's rank controls formal precedence, while their actual work may be diplomatic, judicial, academic, military, or administrative. 01 Chancellor of Narvea 02 Actual Privy Councillor 03 Privy Councillor 04 Actual State Councillor 05 State Councillor Drake's rank 06 Collegiate Councillor RANK AND OFFICE Drake is a State Councillor by rank and an Official for Special Assignments by office. He serves as an elite executive troubleshooter attached to a high-ranking personal office. Free from routine administration, he carries delegated authority into confidential criminal investigations, political counter-espionage, emergency corruption audits, and diplomatic errands. Open Drake's profile → 06 Cultural character Layered, regional, distinctly Narvean Narvean is a shared political identity, not a single ethnicity. Different regions keep their own language, faith, architecture, and historical memory. CIVIC IDENTITY The state is the common ground. Regional, linguistic, religious, urban, and rural communities can all be fully Narvean. INSTITUTIONS Old military customs, ducal administration, civic government, and modern Narvean constitutionalism. FAITH Catholic and Orthodox traditions coexist across different regions. PUBLIC LIFE Baltic merchant culture, old aristocratic ceremony, and modern parliamentary politics. CENTRAL TENSION A modern country that never fully discarded inherited hierarchy. Why it matters to the story Narvea is stable because old and modern power remain in balance. It is also vulnerable for the same reason. Every crisis can become a dispute over who has the right to act, what must remain hidden, and which institution will bear the consequences.
