entries.title: The Magiarchy
entries.text: The Magiarchy # the-magiarchy Magical governance framework Territorial order World / The Magiarchy Territorial magical order A hierarchy that ends at the border The highest official position a Magus can obtain is Magiarch. Each Magiarch oversees magical affairs and relations with the churches inside a defined territory, but no Magiarch may turn that authority into a larger united organization. Highest office Magiarch Jurisdiction One territory Primary relation Magiarchy and churches Higher union Explicitly forbidden 01 Highest office The Magiarch is the ceiling of lawful magical authority OFFICIAL APEX Magiarch The office is usually held by the main Magus assigned to oversee the Magiarchy within a single territorial jurisdiction. 01 Territorial oversight Authority is tied to a defined country or district rather than to a universal magical hierarchy. 02 Church relations The office manages the local relationship between organized Magi and the churches that monitor and counterbalance them. 03 Factional leadership A Magiarch and the Magi aligned with them become a political actor with interests, allies, rivals, and local pressures. RECOGNITION PROCESS Authority is requested, judged, or won Several methods are known, and some carry far more respect than others. 01 Formal application A Magus with a substantial network, friendships, and connections submits a claim to the Church. Church approval gives the office its ordinary seal of legitimacy. 02 Contested decision When several candidates possess credible claims, church authorities and respected Magiarchs from other jurisdictions may share the decision. 03 Fitness contest A deadlock may be settled through a duel or another controlled competition intended to measure fitness for the office. 04 Sanctioned war The radical path permits rival Magi to fight to the death under Church supervision. Innocents cannot be harmed, and the existence of magic must remain hidden from the wider world. RECOGNITION CAN BE WITHDRAWN The Church may revoke recognition and destroy a Magiarch's legitimacy, but it cannot directly install a replacement. The office is independent enough to deny the Church a power of appointment, yet dependent enough that Church disapproval can create a vacancy nobody is automatically empowered to solve. 02 Territorial scale Jurisdiction follows practical size COMMON MODEL One country A single Magiarch may oversee the whole territory when its size and magical population can be managed as one jurisdiction. LARGER TERRITORY One district A large country may be divided into several Magiarchates, each governed within its own district rather than subordinated to a national magical superior. WHO DRAWS THE LINE Church authorities certify Magiarchate boundaries according to practical governability. The same transnational religious hierarchy that prevents Magi from forming a transnational command therefore decides where each supposedly independent magical jurisdiction begins and ends. 03 Structural counterbalance Magiarchal power is fragmented because the churches are not MAGIARCHATES Territorial and separate Magiarchs are explicitly forbidden from uniting into a larger organization. Their lawful authority stops with their territory. COUNTERWEIGHT CHURCHES Organized across borders The churches retain cross-national organization, giving them a wider structure that counterbalances the concentrated power of Magi. WHY THE BAN EXISTS A united organization of Magiarchs would overturn the intended balance and create open conflict with the churches. Examine the church counterweight → 04 Relations without a sovereign Magiarchates exist in an anarchic order NO HIGHER MAGICAL GOVERNMENT There is no lawful authority above the Magiarchs capable of reliably settling disputes between them. Anarchy here does not mean constant chaos. It means the absence of a superior power that can compel every Magiarchate to obey. 01 Self-preservation Each faction must judge threats and protect its own position. 02 Alliance Cooperation depends on interest, trust, and temporary alignment. 03 Rivalry Competing aims can produce pressure resembling conflict between states. 04 Uncertainty No Magiarch can be certain how another faction will use its power. PLAUSIBLE METHOD · NOT CONFIRMED Institutions may penetrate one another Rival Magiarchates, criminal Magi, and church networks may covertly or illegally place operatives, informants, or influence inside one another's structures. If this occurs, visible affiliation cannot be treated as proof of who truly directed an action. 05 Outside the sanctioned order A Magus without jurisdiction becomes a common enemy CRIMINAL STATUS Unbound and unsanctioned A Magus is treated as a criminal when they belong to no territorial jurisdiction and practice outside church supervision or permission. 01 No jurisdiction The Magus does not belong to a recognized Magiarchate. 02 No church sanction Their practice proceeds without church supervision or permission. CHURCH RESPONSE Special envoys The churches use their covert operatives to identify, pursue, and suppress Magi outside the sanctioned order. Examine special envoys → SHARED TARGET MAGIARCH RESPONSE Territorial resources The responsible Magiarch is expected to use the resources under their authority to hunt the same offender. SUPPRESSION DOCTRINE Witness control is a shared responsibility of the Church and Magiarchy, but the Church holds final sanction. Magiarchal resources may carry out coercion, discrediting, forced service, kidnapping, or lethal removal according to circumstance and perceived exposure. Read the doctrine record → UNEASY COOPERATION The pursuit is shared, but trust is not. Church authorities often doubt that a Magiarch will act decisively enough against another Magus. 06 Known office holder Fionn concealed the office behind MSF NARVEA Fionn Secret Magiarch of the country and, in public, director of MSF. His two roles placed magical governance and an ordinary intelligence institution under the same person without revealing their connection. Open Fionn's profile → Open the MSF record → Awaiting definition Open framework questions Who convenes a replacement process after recognition is withdrawn Rules for duels, fitness contests, and sanctioned wars How contested boundary revisions are appealed What customs govern disputes between Magiarchates ✎ Page notes Magiarchy Use notes to define offices and inter-Magiarchate customs without turning open questions into canon.
